     5	import { PLAN_ARCHIVE_FILENAME, SYNTHESIS_ARCHIVE_FILENAME } from '../utils/constants.js';

    15	# Project Ledger MCP — Tool Reference
    16	
    17	## Path Parameters
    18	
    19	**Most tools accept \`project_path\` and/or \`cwd_path\`.** If you have \`project_path\` (the plan folder), use it — it's the fastest path. If you only know your workspace directory, pass \`cwd_path\` and the server auto-detects the active project. If you pass both, \`project_path\` takes precedence and \`cwd_path\` is ignored. The one exception is \`ledger_initialize_project\`, which requires \`project_path\` (the plan folder is being created and cannot be detected yet).
    20	
    21	## All Available Tools
    22	
    23	| Tool | Required Params | Purpose |
    24	|------|----------------|---------|
    25	| ledger_get_project_status | cwd_path or project_path | Read project overview |
    26	| ledger_initialize_project | project_path, plan_file | Create new project ledger |
    27	| ledger_list_projects | None (status filter optional) | List all tracked projects with status, dates, and plan paths |
    28	| ledger_complete_synthesis | cwd_path or project_path | Mark synthesis as generated; transitions project to COMPLETE |
    29	| ledger_get_work_package | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id | Read a work package's full detail |
    30	| ledger_list_work_packages | cwd_path or project_path | List work packages (optional: status, assigned_to filters) |

    32	| ledger_claim_work_package | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, agent | Claim a READY WP → IN_PROGRESS |
    33	| ledger_begin_work | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, agent_role | Claim + start pipeline in one atomic call |
    34	| ledger_update_work_package_status | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, status, agent | Update WP status |
    35	| ledger_start_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type | Start a pipeline for a work package (ordering determined by WP's active_pipeline_stages) |
    36	| ledger_complete_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, status, summary | Complete a pipeline |
    37	| ledger_cancel_pipeline | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, reason | Cancel a stale IN_PROGRESS pipeline (sets to FAIL) |
    38	| ledger_update_pipeline_progress | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, type, summary | Update summary of IN_PROGRESS pipeline without completing it |
    39	| ledger_add_observation | cwd_path or project_path, work_package_id, pipeline_type, type, priority, note | Add observation to pipeline |
    40	| ledger_add_project_comment | cwd_path or project_path, type, priority, agent, note | Add project-level comment |
    41	| ledger_get_next_action | cwd_path or project_path, agent_role | Get next recommended action (optional: max_results for batch mode) |
    42	| ledger_get_handoff_status | cwd_path or project_path, current_agent | Check handoff status |
    43	| ledger_add_insight | scope, title, content, category, tags | Add a reusable insight to the knowledge base |
    44	| ledger_search_insights | query | Search the knowledge base (optional: scope, category, tags, repository_name, limit) |
    45	| ledger_list_insights | None required | List insights with optional filters and pagination |
    46	| ledger_update_insight | id | Update an existing insight by numeric ID |
    47	| ledger_get_repository_context | cwd_path or repository_name | Return project timeline, outcome summaries, insights, and strategic vision for a repository (for Planner agent history access) |
    48	
    49	## Common Mistakes
    50	
    51	1. **Forgetting the "agent" parameter** — ledger_claim_work_package, ledger_update_work_package_status, and ledger_add_project_comment ALL require an "agent" param with your agent name.
    52	2. **Wrong pipeline type names** — Use exactly: "implementation", "qa", "security-audit", "code-review", "release-engineering", "documentation". Only the pipeline types listed in a WP's \`active_pipeline_stages\` are valid for that WP.
    53	3. **Trying to mark COMPLETE as the wrong terminal agent** — Only the agent owning the last active stage of the WP's pipeline can auto-finalize to COMPLETE. For the default 4-stage pipeline this is the Documentation agent. For non-standard compositions (e.g., verification-only \`["qa", "code-review"]\`), it is the agent owning the last active stage (e.g., Reviewer).
    54	4. **Starting a pipeline before claiming the WP** — WP must be IN_PROGRESS before starting a pipeline.
    55	5. **Not updating acceptance_criteria** — Use the acceptance_criteria_updates param in ledger_complete_pipeline to mark criteria as met before marking WP COMPLETE.
    56	6. **Starting pipelines out of order** — Pipelines must follow the WP's active stage order (a subsequence of: implementation → qa → security-audit → code-review → release-engineering → documentation). Starting a stage requires a PASS pipeline on the immediately preceding active stage. Starting a stage not in the WP's \`active_pipeline_stages\` is also rejected.
    57	7. **Setting WP to BLOCKED after a pipeline FAIL** — When QA or Reviewer fails a pipeline, do NOT set the WP to BLOCKED. Leave it as IN_PROGRESS so the Developer can find it via ledger_get_next_action and rework. BLOCKED should only be used for external blockers (missing APIs, pending decisions, etc.).
    58	8. **Test-only WP references non-existent production method** — When creating a WP whose \`active_pipeline_stages\` excludes "implementation" (test-only, verification-only, or documentation-only), verify that all methods/functions referenced in the WP's scope already exist in production code. If they don't, the WP needs the "implementation" stage — otherwise the Developer will silently expand scope by adding production code inside a non-implementation WP.
    59	
    60	## Workflow Order
    61	
    62	1. PM creates work packages (ledger_create_work_package), optionally specifying a custom \`active_pipeline_stages\` to compose the pipeline (defaults to \`["implementation","qa","code-review","documentation"]\`)
    63	2. Developer claims WP and starts pipeline in one call (\`ledger_begin_work\` type="implementation", agent_role="Developer"), completes pipeline (ledger_complete_pipeline). Note: starting a pipeline auto-updates assigned_to on the WP.
    64	3. QA starts pipeline (type="qa"), completes pipeline
    65	3a. *(Optional — only if WP's active_pipeline_stages includes "security-audit")* Security Auditor starts pipeline (type="security-audit"), completes pipeline
    66	4. Reviewer starts pipeline (type="code-review"), completes pipeline
    67	4a. *(Optional — only if WP's active_pipeline_stages includes "release-engineering")* Release Engineer starts pipeline (type="release-engineering"), completes pipeline
    68	5. Documentation starts pipeline (type="documentation"), completes pipeline — if status=PASS and all acceptance criteria are met, the WP is automatically transitioned to COMPLETE (auto-finalize, no separate ledger_update_work_package_status call needed)
    69	
    70	**Note:** The terminal agent (owner of the last active stage) triggers auto-finalize on PASS. For non-standard compositions (e.g., \`["qa","code-review"]\`), the Reviewer is the terminal agent who auto-finalizes the WP to COMPLETE.
    71	
    72	**Important:** Every ledger_complete_pipeline response includes a "--- NEXT STEP ---" guidance block telling you exactly what to do next. Follow it.
    73	
    74	## Rework After Pipeline FAIL
    75	
    76	When a QA or code-review pipeline completes with FAIL:
    77	- The agent who ran the failing pipeline should leave the WP as IN_PROGRESS (do NOT set to BLOCKED)
    78	- Call ledger_get_handoff_status to confirm handoff
    79	- The Developer will automatically see a REWORK action via ledger_get_next_action
    80	- The Developer re-implements, then the pipeline chain continues from QA again
    81	
    82	## Handoff Block Format
    83	
    84	Every agent must end their response with the handoff block returned by ledger_get_handoff_status. The block uses three fields:
    85	
    86	\`\`\`
    87	CURRENT AGENT: <current_agent>
    88	NEXT AGENT: <next_agent>
    89	STATUS: <status>
    90	\`\`\`
    91	
    92	- **current_agent**: The agent that just finished working (you)
    93	- **next_agent**: The agent that should pick up work next (derived from status)
    94	- **status**: The workflow status (e.g., READY_FOR_QA, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE)
    95	
    96	All three fields are returned by ledger_get_handoff_status — copy them verbatim.
    97	
    98	## Action Tool max_results
    99	
   100	- **ledger_get_next_action** (singular, default): Returns the first actionable WP for your role. Best for simple projects or when you process one WP at a time.

   907	  ledger_get_repository_context: `
   908	# ledger_get_repository_context
   909	
   910	Returns a compact project timeline with curated outcome summaries, relevant knowledge-base insights,
   911	and strategic vision for a repository. Gives the **Planner agent** access to prior project history
   912	within the same repository so it can make context-aware planning decisions.
   913	
   914	## When to Call
   915	
   916	Call this at the start of a planning session to understand:
   917	- What projects have been worked on in this repository and their outcomes
   918	- The repository's declared strategic vision (if configured)
   919	- Relevant global and repository-scoped knowledge-base insights
   920	
   921	## Required Parameters (at least one of these must be provided)
   922	- **cwd_path** (string): Absolute path to the workspace root directory. The server derives the
   923	  repository name from this path using the same logic as project auto-detection. Use this when you
   924	  know your workspace directory but haven't set an explicit repository name.
   925	- **repository_name** (string): Explicit repository name to look up in the registry. When provided,
   926	  \`cwd_path\` is not used for name derivation. Takes precedence over \`cwd_path\` if both are given.
   927	
   928	## Optional Parameters
   929	- **include_insights** (boolean, default: \`true\`): When \`true\`, the response includes a
   930	  \`relevant_insights[]\` array populated from both the global and repository-scoped knowledge stores.
   931	  Set to \`false\` to skip knowledge-store queries and return an empty array — useful when you only
   932	  need the project timeline and want a smaller response.
   933	- **max_projects** (integer, positive, default: \`5\`): Maximum number of projects to include in
   934	  the \`projects[]\` array. Projects are sorted by \`date_created\` descending (most recent first),
   935	  so this cap retains the most recent history. Increase this if you need deeper historical context.
   936	
   937	## Response Shape
   938	\`\`\`json
   939	{
   940	  "repository_name": "ai-insights",
   941	  "repository_id": "repo-uuid-or-null",
   942	  "repository_label": "AI Insights (human-readable label or null)",
   943	  "total_projects": 12,
   944	  "strategic_vision": {
   945	    "summary": "Build an agentic ledger system...",
   946	    "goals": ["Goal A", "Goal B"],
   947	    "constraints": ["Constraint A"]
   948	  },
   949	  "projects": [
   950	    {
   951	      "slug": "2026-05-20-feature-x",
   952	      "plan_path": "/path/to/plans/2026-05-20-feature-x",
   953	      "status": "COMPLETE",
   954	      "date_created": "2026-05-20T10:00:00Z",
   955	      "last_updated": "2026-05-25T14:30:00Z",
   956	      "title": "Feature X",
   957	      "outcome_summary": "Implemented X using Y approach. All 35 tests pass.",
   958	      "progress_pct": 100
   959	    }
   960	  ],
   961	  "relevant_insights": [
   962	    {
   963	      "id": 1,
   964	      "formatted_id": "KN-0001",
   965	      "scope": "global",
   966	      "title": "Always validate slugs at the schema boundary",
   967	      "content": "...",
   968	      "category": "security",
   969	      "tags": ["security", "validation"]
   970	    }
   971	  ]
   972	}
   973	\`\`\`
   974	
   975	### Response Field Details
   976	
   977	| Field | Type | Description |
   978	|-------|------|-------------|
   979	| \`repository_name\` | string | Derived or supplied repository identifier |
   980	| \`repository_id\` | string \| null | Registry UUID, or \`null\` if no registry entry found |
   981	| \`repository_label\` | string \| null | Human-readable label from the registry, or \`null\` |
   982	| \`total_projects\` | number | Total number of projects found across all matched folder names |
   983	| \`strategic_vision\` | object \| null | Vision block from the registry entry, or \`null\` if not configured |
   984	| \`projects[]\` | array | Up to \`max_projects\` most recent projects (see Project Entry fields below) |
   985	| \`relevant_insights[]\` | array | Global + repository-scoped insights (empty array when \`include_insights: false\`) |
   986	
   987	### Project Entry Fields
   988	
   989	| Field | Type | Description |
   990	|-------|------|-------------|
   991	| \`slug\` | string | Directory slug (e.g., \`2026-05-20-feature-x\`) |
   992	| \`plan_path\` | string | Original \`project_path\` used during initialization |
   993	| \`status\` | string | Current project status: READY, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETE, BLOCKED |
   994	| \`date_created\` | string | ISO 8601 creation timestamp |
   995	| \`last_updated\` | string | ISO 8601 last-updated timestamp |
   996	| \`title\` | string? | Optional human-readable title (omitted when not set) |
   997	| \`outcome_summary\` | string \| null | 2–3 sentence synthesis summary (set by the Synthesis agent via \`ledger_complete_synthesis\`); \`null\` when no synthesis has been generated |
   998	| \`progress_pct\` | number? | Completion percentage 0–100 (omitted when not available) |
   999

  1001	
  1002	When the resolved repository name matches a declared registry entry that lists multiple
  1003	\`folder_names\`, the tool reads projects from **all** matching folder names and merges the results
  1004	into a single sorted list. This ensures projects stored across aliased repository directories
  1005	(e.g., the same repo renamed or reorganised) all appear in the timeline.
  1006	
  1007	## Examples

  1012	  "cwd_path": "/Users/name/projects/my-repo"
  1013	}

  1020	}
  1021	\`\`\`
  1022	
  1023	### Deeper history, no insights
  1024	\`\`\`json
  1025	{

   702	
   703	Call this after the Synthesis agent has finished generating its synthesis report. Subsequent calls to \`ledger_get_next_action(Synthesis)\` will return WAIT once this flag is set.
   704	
   705	The synthesis document is automatically archived into the ledger storage directory on
   706	completion. If the file does not exist, it is silently skipped and reported in
   707	\`archive_skipped\`.
   708

   710	${CWD_PATH_PARAM}
   711	${PROJECT_PATH_PARAM}
   712	- **outcome_summary** (string): A 2–3 sentence summary of what was accomplished, the approach taken, and any notable results or limitations. This value is persisted to both \`project-ledger.json\` (root index) and the \`.meta.json\` enrichment cache, and is echoed back in the success response.
   713	
   714	## Optional Parameters
   715	- **synthesis_file** (string, default: \`"${SYNTHESIS_ARCHIVE_FILENAME}"\`): Filename of the synthesis
   716	  document relative to project_path. Defaults to \`${SYNTHESIS_ARCHIVE_FILENAME}\`; specify an alternative
   717	  filename if your Synthesis agent writes to a different file.
   718	
   719	## Response Fields
   720	- **synthesis_generated** (boolean): Always \`true\`
